key_highlights: ASX finished flat as miners rose but oil stocks struggled; IDP plunged on sector-specific weakness (#33)
RBA signals further rate hikes as inflation pressures test central bank credibility, squeezing household spending (#21, #53)
Australian flash PMI sags, signalling softening economic momentum (#47)
Oil prices jump on tightening global buffers, raising fuel cost fears for Australia (#16, #30)
Bond market pressure rattles Wall Street, creating cross-asset volatility spilling into ASX (#16)
Rare earths and gold names surge: Critica offtake progress, Critical Resources Suriname grab, Aurum $52.5M raise (#36, #37, #38)
Tech stocks lead ASX higher post Wall Street surge; OpenAI-Medicare breach dominates headlines (#70, #1, #8)
Property market weakens: rising listings and falling demand push prices lower (#39)
Jetstar industrial action escalates with staff waiving baggage/seat fees (#67, #69)
Federal and state governments face mounting debt pressures (#73)

sectors.trend: Miners outperform as rare earths and gold names surge; Critica offtake, Critical Resources Suriname gold, Aurum $52.5M raise drive small-cap momentum. China's rebalancing towards robots supports industrial metals demand. Oil stocks lag despite higher crude.
sectors.implications: Rotation into small/mid-cap resource names; BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from broad commodity strength but oil-linked names (WDS.AX, WLE.AX) face margin pressure. Rare earths (CRS.AX, JPR.AX) and gold (AUG.AX, CRG.AX) offer thematic upside.

sectors.trend: RBA rate hike cycle continues, compressing household spending and raising NIM pressures. Bond market volatility from Wall Street spillover creates mark-to-market risk. Government debt concerns add sovereign risk premium.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates but face credit cycle risk as household spending tightens. Watch NIM vs. provision balance. Government debt trajectory (#73) pressures sovereign bond yields.

sectors.trend: Oil prices jump on drying global buffers; fuel cost fears intensify for Australia. Nuclear energy debate gains traction. Data centre power demand strains net-zero targets. Political energy cost disputes (Labor vs Coalition) add noise.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX benefit from higher crude but face political headwinds. Renewable/energy transition names (SOL.AX, LNC.AX) gain from nuclear debate and data centre demand. Fuel cost pass-through pressures consumer sector.

sectors.trend: Tech leads ASX higher post Wall Street surge. OpenAI-Medicare breach raises cybersecurity and data governance concerns. $16B Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy. Data centre build-out accelerates.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (WTC.AX, XRO.AX, NEG.AX) benefit from global tech rally. Cybersecurity and data governance themes gain relevance. China-linked tech exposure (e.g., #32) faces regulatory risk. Equinix-type data centre plays (EQIX) relevant for AI infrastructure.

sectors.trend: RBA hikes squeeze household spending. Jetstar industrial action escalates. Qantas announces Sydney-New York non-stop. EV adoption accelerates with Chinese 5-min battery tech. Middle-income inequality widens.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces Jetstar (JST.AX) competitive and industrial risk. WES.AX, WOW.AX pressured by tight household budgets. EV supply chain (Chinese battery #9) disrupts local auto sector. Consumer staples defensive appeal rises.

sectors.trend: Rising listings and falling demand drive property prices lower. Chinese property recovery uncertain. Data centre REITs benefit from AI build-out but face net-zero scrutiny.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICV.AX) face oversupply risk. Data centre/infrastructure REITs (VGE.AX, STP.AX) gain from AI demand. Chinese property recovery (#40) a watch item for commodity-linked REITs.

sectors.trend: Syngenis gains precision medicine firepower. Medicare data breach (OpenAI) raises healthcare data security concerns. Mental health screening policy debate.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. SYG.AX benefits from precision medicine expansion. Healthcare IT/cybersecurity names gain from Medicare breach narrative.

Commodity rotation: oil up, rare earths/gold surging, China robot rebalancing

risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain liquidity buffers; hedge duration risk; monitor AUD/USD and 10yr GBA yields

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight energy producers (WDS.AX, WLE.AX); underweight transport and consumer discretionary

risk_assessment.risk_factor: China geopolitical and trade risk (tech links, Indo-Pacific)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from China-revenue-dependent ASX names; monitor China property recovery signals

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Industrial action (Jetstar) and labour market disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid JST.AX near-term; monitor QAN.AX competitive positioning

defensive_moves.rationale: Rising listings, falling demand, and higher rates pressure valuations; Chinese property recovery uncertain

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight consumer discretionary and transport on household spending squeeze
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA hikes compress disposable income; Jetstar industrial action; fuel costs rising

defensive_moves.rationale: Wall Street bond pressure, government debt concerns, and RBA uncertainty create tail risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hold CSL.AX and consumer staples as defensive anchors
defensive_moves.rationale: Healthcare and staples provide stability amid rate volatility and spending compression

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to trade in a narrow range with sector rotation. Miners and tech provide upside; oil stocks, REITs, and consumer face headwinds. RBA rate path and bond market volatility are dominant drivers. PMI softness (#47) and household spending squeeze (#53) cap upside. Oil spike supports energy but pressures transport and consumer. Expect elevated volatility into month-end.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA peaks and inflation moderates. Structural themes: AI/data centre build-out, energy transition (nuclear, EVs), rare earths supply chain, and China rebalancing. Property oversupply and fiscal sustainability remain overhangs. ASX 200 likely to grind higher on earnings if rate cycle eases, but government debt and global risk-off episodes create volatility.
